title: gm-delegate instrumentation record
description: NORMATIVE. Spec §6. One record per card, from the first commit. This is the labelled dataset that §9's kill criteria are computed from, so a missing field is a hole in your go/no-go decision. Validate on write; a rejected record is a bug to fix now, not a record to drop.

intent_id.description: The ULID from the envelope (§5.6). Joins this record to the wire trace.

proposal_id.description: Present whenever a card was rendered. Joins to proposal.schema.json.

mode.description: The mode in force when this fired. Needed to interpret the accept rate: an accept under 'auto' is not the same signal as an accept under 'propose'.

type.description: v1 only ever emits gm_command (§4.7) and hook (§4.6). 'watcher' is v2.

selected.description: Actor id of the controlled token. §4.6 calls controlToken the highest-signal event in the system, so this column carries most of the predictive weight.

entity_link.description: UUID of the linked catalog document, or null for chatter. v2 (§7.3); always null in v1.

model.description: Exact served model string, e.g. 'qwen3.5-9b-q4km'. §10 picks the model from this column.

total.description: GM prompt to card on screen. §9 threshold is a median under 5000.

tool_calls.description: Needed for §9's tool-call validity threshold (>95%). Without this array that kill criterion cannot be computed.

gm_action.description: accept=positive. edit=positive plus a quality signal. reroll=weak negative. skip=weak negative. expired=negative (never opened). See §6's label table.

gm_edit_diff.description: The distance between the model's register and yours. §5.4 calls this the best training signal in the system.

rejected.description: Present when the Interceptor refused. §8 M2 is proved by finding these in the log.
